newsitem.title: QATAR: Manila undecided on fate Filipina maid film.
newsitem.headline: Manila undecided on fate Filipina maid film.

text.p: The fate of a controversial film about a Moslem Filipina maid who escaped execution in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) is still undecided, Philippines President Fidel Ramos said on Sunday.
"Film is film, we have not taken any decision," Ramos who is on a two-day official visit to Qatar told Reuters.
"The Foreign Office is considering it, we do not want to offend anybody's feelings, especially our friends'," he added.
Officials in Manila said on Friday the film failed to premier after the Foreign Office ruled its screening could harm ties with the UAE.

Film director Joel Lamangan accused the Philippines Movie and Television Review and Classification Board (MTRCB) of abuse of power after it refused to release a permit for the public exhibition of the film "Sarah Balabagan Story".
The film is based on the story of teenager Balabagan, who was sentenced to death by a UAE court for stabbing to death her Arab employer in 1994. Balabagan claimed her employer had tried to rape her.
The sentence was reduced to one year in jail and 100 lashes after UAE President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan intervened.

Balabagan and the film's cast arrived at a Manila cinema on Thursday evening for the premiere, but left disappointed after being told the MTRCB had refused to release a permit for the film's screening.
A Philippines Foreign Office spokesman said earlier that showing the film could adversely affect the good relations between the UAE and the Philippines. spokesman
About 80,000 Filipinos work in the UAE.
